reasons: The original statement requires a whitespace-exact checker: 'Note that in this problem the checker checks your answer taking spaces into consideration. Do not print any extra characters.' Every output line must contain exactly sum(a_i) characters from {'/', '\\', ' '}. The repo judge and pipeline/checker.py compare whitespace-split tokens (docs/JUDGE_API.md 'Token-based comparison'), so a token comparison would be falsely unique: it accepts images with wrong column positions, missing leading or trailing padding, or extra space columns.

Selected public CF WRONG_ANSWER sources would pass a token checker even though they fail CF's whitespace check. They were inspected, not executed. 49683913 (WA, passedTestCount 0) builds the correct image but trims each row after its last non-space character, so it drops the required trailing spaces. 151394193 (WA, passedTestCount 0) writes columns 1..S of 1001-wide rows, so every row gets an extra leading space and is padded to 1001 characters. Neither output differs from the correct image in its token sequence. Using those verdicts as algorithmic WA evidence, or treating token-AC as faithful, would be wrong.

The upstream test bytes cannot back an exact checker either. 15 of the 43 pinned official outputs (all of the LF-stored large cases) are missing the leading spaces of line 1 (listed in officialReview.malformedOrContradictoryPairs), so a correct program fails them under exact comparison. The pinned row's examples have lost all spaces and line structure. The statement itself says the sample answers cannot be copied and links to assets.codeforces.com/rounds/435/{1,2}.txt.

Any trustworthy package would need a custom whitespace-exact checker plus authored, re-derived expected outputs to replace the corrupted official bytes. This author task forbids both rewriting imported test bytes to fit a solver and making token comparison falsely unique, so the recipe is excluded instead of authored. No recipe_435C.py or test_recipe_435C.py was written.
exclusion.reversal: Feasible only if the parent decides to add a whitespace-exact checker contract (specialJudge/custom checker) and accepts authored expected outputs in place of the 15 malformed official outputs. The derivation used here (rows y = max..min+1; up-segment k of edge i puts '/' at column x_i+k in row y_i+k, down-segment puts '\\' at column x_i+k in row y_i-k) reproduces the other 28 official outputs exactly, and both attached sample answer files byte-for-byte.
